content.text: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Quietly Discussed an AI Safety Standards Body: The September 13 report said Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google had been discussing an industry standards body. It also reported that OpenAI CEO Sam Altman favored the labs creating such a body without U.S. government support, while a White House draft effort had stalled. The report relied on people familiar with the discussions. (time=2026-09-13T19:16:00Z; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).

Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Quietly Discussed an AI Safety Standards Body: The September 13 report said Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google had been discussing an industry standards body. It also reported that OpenAI CEO Sam Altman favored the labs creating such a body without U.S. government support, while a White House draft effort had stalled. The report relied on people familiar with the discussions. (time=2026-09-13T19:16:00Z; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
Truth Social Posts of September 24, 2026: The archive dates Trump's pre-summit post to 7:24 a.m. ET on September 24 and links to its Truth Social record. The post described AI as a summit topic, said he wanted to leave it where it was, characterized that as China's position, and identified the DOJ as the U.S. guardrail. (time=2026-09-24T11:24:00Z; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
AI Companies and World Leaders Race to Write Safety Rules: The September 24 article says 22 international leaders had called for exploring a UN role in AI oversight, but that the statement did not create an institution. It also reports that OpenAI publicly supported voluntary industry standards as well as mandatory U.S. safety requirements. The article says the proposed private body's name remained tentative and its membership, powers, and standards had not been publicly announced. (time=2026-09-24; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
